newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian opposition says protester beaten in jail.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition says protester beaten in jail.

text.p: Lawyers for the Serbian opposition protesting against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic said on Sunday that one of their supporters has been badly beaten by police in prison.

"The most dramatic of all arrests was that of the young man who carried an effigy of Milosevic in stripped prison clothes. He was severely beaten, tortured in prison," Nikola Barovic, member of the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition legal board, told a news conference on Sunday.

Barovic was referring to Dejan Bulatovic, a 21-year old worker from the northeast town of Sid. Shots of Bulatovic carrying the two-meter (seven-foot) tall effigy during the street demonstrations in Belgrade captured world attention.
The opposition has staged daily protests attracting up to 150,000 people against the annulment of its victories at local elections last month.
The annulment drew sharp criticism from the West, which has piled pressure on Milosevic to respect democracy.
Bulatovic was arrested on Friday hours after the demonstrations were over and when he was walking to his home in the Karaburma workers district of Belgrade.
"No defence attorney has yet been allowed in to see him," Barovic said.

"Over the past week 40 protesters were arrested. None were allowed defence counsel, apart from one case. Many of those arrested were kept in police custody longer than the 24 hours legally permitted," Barovic said.
He said Zajedno received information about Bulatovic's injuries from other prisoners who saw him in jail but were released on later Saturday.
He said the released prisoners spoke of head and chest fractures to Dejan's body.
"The police themselves called the emergency to check if he would not die on them in prison," he said.
Barovic said Bulatovic was suffering from chronic lung and bronchial desease and was released from the army due to his condition.
Bulatovic was transported to the Belgrade central jail on Saturday.
Barovic then quoted from a letter by Dejan's mother Ljiljana Bulatovic who was allowed to see her son in central prison.
"She said she found her son naked on a cement floor in a cell with a window that could not be shut.

"He had difficulty dressing himself, breathing. He had a broken nose. He said they put a gun barrel in his mouth and threatened to shoot him. He was given papers printed in 1989 to read," Barovic said.
There was no official comment on Barovic's allegations.
